summary: If you are resident and paid for the treatment of a prescribed disease or ailment for yourself or a dependant, the amount paid is deducted up to a limit, larger where the person treated is a senior citizen. What an insurer paid or an employer reimbursed for it is taken off first. Only the old regime allows it.

routes.name: Treatment for you or a dependant
routes.description: The amount paid, less what was insured or reimbursed, up to the limit.

routes.name: Treatment for a senior citizen
routes.description: The larger limit where the person treated is a senior citizen.

disqualifiers.description: It is not deducted in the default regime.
Treatment for a senior citizen and for someone who is not, in the same year, is not computed.

enforcedBy.reason: which limit applies is not settled

disqualifiers.description: A Hindu undivided family's claim under this deduction is not computed.

enforcedBy.reason: the deduction for a Hindu undivided family is not built
